To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prolonged activation of N-methyl-D-Asp (NMDA)-receptors in hippocampal dentrate granule neurons reduces GABA-A-receptor (GABAAR) δ-subunit expression, and this reduction in expression is associated with a decrease in the surface expression of both δ- and α4-subunits.

prolonged activation of N-methyl-D- aspartate receptors in cultured hippocampal dentategyranule neurons reduces the expression of δ subunit-containing γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors by mechanisms involving calcium entry and activation of extracellular signal- regulated kinases 1/2.

activation of NMDARs in hippocampal dentategyrus neurons reduces the expression of GABAAδ subunits, which results in reduced tonic inhibition and reduced sensitivity to positive modulators of GABAergic neurotransmission, such as neurosteroids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mechanism by which GABARs are modified in the epileptic brain.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the downregulation of GABARs containing the δ subunit, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of epilepsy.
the molecular basis of the reduced expression of δ subunits in epileptic animals and the resulting reduction of GABAR sensitivity to neurosteroids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NMDA receptor-mediated downregulation of δ-subunit-containing GABAA receptors in the hippocampus is a consequence of the increased excitatory activity and that this downregulation may contribute to the development of the epilepsy.
prolonged NMDA receptor activation downregulated GABAA receptor δ subunit expression in hippocampal dentrate granule cells through a Ca2+/ERK1/2-dependent mechanism.
prolonged NMDA receptor activation downregulates expression of δ subunit-containing GABAA receptors in cultured hippocampal dentates through Ca2+ and ERK1/ 2 activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prolonged activation of N-methyl-D-Asp receptors in cultured hippocampal granule neurons downregulates the expression of δ subunit containing GABAA receptors by Ca2+ and ERK1/ 2 dependent mechanism.

prolonged activation of N-methyl-D-Asp receptors (NMDAR) in hippocampal cultures downregulates expression of δ-subunit containing GABAA receptors through Ca2+-dependent and extracellular signal regulated kinase-dependent mechanisms, which may be involved in the plasticity of hippocampal GABAA receptors observed in epileptic animals.
NMDA receptor activation leads to a decrease in the number of GABAA receptor δ subunits in hippocampal granule neurons and thus reduces the sensitivity of these receptors to neurosteroids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptor activation downregulates GABAR δ expression and reduces the tonic current in hippocampal granule cells.
NMDA activation can trigger a decrease in the expression of δ-containing GABARs, which is consistent with the reduced neurosteroid sensitivity of hippocampal GABARs in epileptic animals.

the reduction of δ subunit-containing GABARs in dentate granule cells of epileptic animals may be a consequence of the prolonged activation of N-methyl-D- aspartic acid ( NMDA) receptors in these neurons.
